# PromptShelf

> A local-first library to save, template, reuse and share prompts. Prompts are Markdown files with YAML frontmatter, in folders the person owns, synced with plain git. The `shelf` command finds and fills them for people and for AI agents. No server, no account, no telemetry. MIT licence.

Key facts for agents:

- Always pass `--json` to `shelf`. Prompt IDs look like `personal/strict-pr-review`; a bare ID works when it is unique.
- Agents can read, fill and save drafts to the Inbox. Other writes (creating a library, pinning, editing, syncing) need a person, and `shelf` exits with code 5 when an agent tries them. Ask the person to run those commands. Do not work around the refusal.
- Never edit library files directly. Save new prompts with `shelf save`, which puts them in the person's Inbox.
- Apps with no shell connect through `shelf mcp`, an MCP server on stdio.

Main commands:

- `shelf search <words> --json`: ranked matches with their blanks.
- `shelf list --json [--lib <name>] [--kind template] [--tag <tag>]`: every prompt, with filters.
- `shelf show <id> --json`: one prompt, its body and its blanks (`vars`).
- `shelf fill <id> --json --var name=value`: exit code 0 means `text` is ready; exit code 3 means `missing` lists the open blanks. Fill them from the conversation, then run it again.
- `shelf save --title "<title>" --json < file`: saves a draft to the Inbox.
- `shelf skill print`: the full instructions for agents (the same text as the Claude Code skill).

## Set up

- [Install PromptShelf](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ETSoftwareStudio/promptshelf/main/docs/agents/install.md): step-by-step instructions for an agent to install `shelf`, create the library with the person, and learn the commands.
- [Connect over MCP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ETSoftwareStudio/promptshelf/main/docs/agents/mcp.md): step-by-step instructions for an agent to add `shelf mcp` to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex or another MCP app.
